AGENDA

  CITY COUNCIL/PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  Monday, December 17, 2018
  Council Chambers
  2000 Main Street
  Huntington Beach, CA 92648

  Study Session - 3:30 PM / Closed Session - 5:00 PM
  Regular Meeting - 6:00 PM

  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
  ERIK PETERSON, Mayor

MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the
hearing impaired, American Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and/or large print agendas. Please
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

AUDIO/VIDEO ACCESS TO BROADCASTED MEETINGS: City Council and Planning Commission meetings are televised live
on HBTV-3 Channel 3, and can be viewed via live or archived website at https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com.

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager introduced Chief Financial Officer Gilbert Garcia who presented a PowerPoint presentation jointly with Acting Director of Community Services Chris Slama entitled: City of Huntington Beach, Master Fee and Charges Schedule and Other Revenue Adjustments, with slides titled: Budget Balancing Review, Summary of Proposed Fee Changes, Proposed Fee Changes Comparison, Community Services History of Parking Meter Rates, Proposed Fee Changes Comparison by Department, Proposed MFS Changes by Department, Proposed Master Fee Changes Community Services Summary, Community Services Special Events Fees (2), Community Services Parking Meter Rates, Proposed MFS Changes Finance Department Summary, Finance Department Entertainment Permits, Finance Department Massage Fees, Finance Department Entertainment & Massage Fee Survey, Proposed MFS Changes Fire Department Summary, Fire Department Inspection and Plan Review Fees, Fire Department Marine Safety Fees, Police Department Parking Citations, Police Department Parking Citations Survey, Community Development Environmental Review (2), and Recommended Actions.\par
\par
Councilmember Delgieize: questioned fee percentages and website availability to the public for our fees.\par
\par
Councilmember Hardy: questioned regarding massage establishment fees and was under the assumption 100% recovered costs in this scenario.\par
\par
MPT Semeta - would like to see no increase resident non-profits.  she also confirmed set-up fees for room rentals are not changing.  \par
\par
Councilmember Brenden - commented re: councilmember Hardy's concern re: massage establishments and does not feel it is fair to penalize one particular type of business.  He reviewed several fee changes and expressed his opinions and thanked staff.\par
\par
Councilmember Carr: questioned staff regarding set-up/take-down special event fees and clarified increases that would affect vendors of large events.  She also expressed possible confusion regarding the published fee schedule and wants fee schedule to be transparent.\par
\par
Mayor Peterson - likes the take/down event fee, and would like to see a more simplified fee schedule on the website.\par
}

\par

\par
Councilmember Brenden: expressed his support in exiting PCTA and it being the prudent way to go for the citizens and the city.\par
\par
Councilmember Delgleize: Questioned staff regarding a possible problem of creating revenue for city. Staff believes we could provide better more relevant content.  \par
\par
Hardy: Questioned staff how vulnerable to budget cuts? Previous issues discussed from 2003 were not funded by PCTA, but was from city funds.\par

return in January to formally withdraw\par
